newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs up after Japan industrial data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs up after Japan industrial data.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures gained sharply on Thursday after the release of lower-than-expected Japan industrial output data.
Dealers said rumours about the lower figures spurred buying even before their official release.
"The markets jumped up on short covering, but generally we are still overshadowed by bearish fundamentals," a dealer with a European commission house said.
Japan's industrial production in April fell 0.4 percent from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis against market forecasts of a rise of between 0.3 percent and 1.5 percent.
The trading band in December Euroyen was especially wide, at more than 14 points, but some dealers said speculative trading was mostly over and the contract could head lower.
"On a quarter-to-quarter basis, it's not weak. People still believe in a rate hike after the tankan report," another dealer with a Japanese financial house said.
The lead December Euroyen contract rose to a high of 98.90 after trading as low as 98.76. At 1115 GMT, December was at 98.87 compared with its previous IMM close at 98.79.
JGBs also rose on hectic short covering, after being sold on Wednesday due to speculation of stronger economic numbers.

Traders said the possibility of an early rise in the discount rate -- as the Bank of Japan announced the earlier release of the tankan report to June 25 -- coupled with a likely U.S. rate hike in the third quarter, had dampened JGBs earlier.
June JGBs settled at 123.58 against a low of 122.32 and a previous close at 122.60.
In Eurodollars, activity was lacklustre ahead of Thursday's jobless claims and non-farm payrolls figures on June 6, critical to whether the Federal Reserve would move to raise rates.
September ended at 93.930 against the IMM's 93.925.
